::: {.hero}
A graduate course on the fundamentals of Bayesian inference and its application
to (high-dimensional) datasets in economics and finance. We pair the theoretical
foundations with hands-on empirical implementation in **Python**.
:::

## At a glance

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.fr-card}
### Format
90-minute lecture (2 SWS) and an exercise session (2 SWS) per week. 6 ECTS. Taught in English.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}

### What you learn
Subjective probability, MCMC, shrinkage priors, BVARs, state-space models,
stochastic volatility, and Bayesian machine learning.

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}

Derive Bayesian updates, implement core algorithms in Python, and use statistical libraries for more complex models.

## What the course is about

Bayesian methods treat unknown parameters as random and combine prior beliefs with
data through the likelihood. That single idea gives a coherent way to quantify
uncertainty, pool information, and regularise large models. This course builds the
machinery from the ground up, then applies it to problems where it has a real
advantage: forecasting with many predictors, modelling time-varying dynamics in
macroeconomics, estimating volatility in finance, and inferring causal effects in
microeconomics.

The emphasis is modern and practical. You will not just read about Gibbs samplers
and Metropolis-Hastings; you will write them. By the end you should have a working
toolbox and the judgment to use it critically.
